payload.root_cause: In src/text.js, the slugify() function's whitespace/dash-collapsing step uses a non-global regex: `.replace(/[\s-]+/, '-')` at line 11 is missing the `g` flag. String.prototype.replace with a non-global regex replaces only the first match, so only the first run of whitespace/dashes is converted to a dash; every subsequent gap remains as-is. For the failing input 'Hello Big  World!', after toLowerCase/trim/stripping '!' the string is 'hello big  world'; only the single space after 'hello' is replaced, producing 'hello-big  world' (the double space between 'big' and 'world' is untouched), exactly the reported actual value. Adding the `g` flag (/[\s-]+/g) would make every run collapse into a single dash, matching the documented contract in the function's docstring (line 4) and README ('words joined by single dashes'). Note line 10 and line 12 correctly use global flags, so this is an isolated flag omission.

payload.rationale: The root cause is the missing `g` flag on the whitespace/dash-collapsing regex in slugify(). `String.prototype.replace` with a non-global regex only substitutes the first match, so in 'Hello Big  World!' → 'hello big  world' only the single space after 'hello' became a dash, leaving the double space between 'big' and 'world' intact ('hello-big  world'). Adding the global flag (/[\s-]+/g) makes every run of whitespace and/or dashes collapse into a single dash, so the output becomes 'hello-big-world' and '  Already-slugged  title ' becomes 'already-slugged-title', matching the function's documented contract ("words joined by single dashes") and the adjacent replaces on lines 10 and 12 which already use global regexes. This is the smallest possible change: one character in the regex literal.
